answer: Since the signal liability is recorded with the signature, the spiral audit exposes who vouched, and self-sponsorship costs more than it saves. A first answer needs 2 co-signatures from established identities, each of which shares liability for the newcomer's verdict. A farm has to recruit that support from outside its own cluster, because an internal co-signature is flagged on the dune graph and the sponsor's bond is exposed. That is 36 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
